headline_marked: Abu Sayed case: [[Four convicted accused file appeals]] for acquittal
headline: Abu Sayed case: Four convicted accused file appeals for acquittal
summary: Two death row convicts and two others sentenced to prison terms have approached the Supreme Court seeking to overturn their convictions in the killing of the BRUR student.
details: Four convicted individuals in the Abu Sayed killing case have filed two separate appeals with the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court, seeking acquittal from the charges.
The convicts include former Rangpur Metropolitan Police assistant sub-inspector Amir Hossain and constable Sujan Chandra Roy, both of whom were sentenced to death.

Also filing appeals are former Begum Rokeya University (BRUR) assistant registrar Rafiul Hasan Russell and Bangladesh Chhatra League joint general secretary Emran Chowdhury, both sentenced to five years' imprisonment.
Abu Sayed, a student of BRUR, was shot dead by police on July 16, 2024, at Park Mor in front of the university during the anti-quota protests.
The convictions were handed down on April 9 this year by the International Crimes Tribunal-2, which sentenced two individuals to death, three to life imprisonment, and 25 others to jail terms.
The death row convicts, Amir and Sujan, filed one joint appeal, while Rafiul and Emran filed another, as they remain in jail.

headline_marked: Nahid Islam [[calls for swift execution of verdict]] in Abu Sayed case
headline: Nahid Islam calls for swift execution of verdict in Abu Sayed case
summary: National Citizen Party Convener Nahid Islam urges the government to bring back Sheikh Hasina and implement the death sentence in the Abu Sayed killing case.
details: National Citizen Party Convener and opposition chief whip Nahid Islam visited the grave of Abu Sayed in Babanpara village, Pirganj, Rangpur, to pay tribute.
Nahid described Abu Sayed's death on July 16, 2024, as a turning point that transformed the student-public movement into a mass uprising.
He called for the swift implementation of the trial court's verdict in the Abu Sayed murder case, noting that an appeal is currently pending.
Nahid identified Sheikh Hasina as the principal accused in the case and stated that she has been sentenced to death by the court.
He expressed hope that the government would bring her back to the country to ensure the verdict is executed.
Beyond the legal case, Nahid emphasized the need for state reforms based on the July referendum and the promised July Charter.
He alleged that the government has failed to make progress on these reforms, despite public support for a discrimination-free and justice-based state.
caption:

He called for the swift implementation of the trial court's verdict in the Abu Sayed murder case, noting that an appeal is currently pending.

Nahid identified Sheikh Hasina as the principal accused in the case and stated that she has been sentenced to death by the court.

He expressed hope that the government would bring her back to the country to ensure the verdict is executed.

He alleged that the government has failed to make progress on these reforms, despite public support for a discrimination-free and justice-based state.
